title: Web builder hands Claude Code a website, ad accounts and budget to run every 4 hours
summary: A website builder gave Claude Code a baseline site, ad accounts on Google, X, LinkedIn and Reddit, a budget and scraping tools, letting it make decisions every four hours. So far it mostly churns out SEO pages and share buttons.
agent_role: Claude Code edits the site and manages ad campaigns on a recurring four-hour schedule; the human set up access and budget and watches.
outcome: Author reports the agent mostly does 'tomfoolery' such as creating many SEO pages and adding share buttons to try to go viral.
what_they_did: A developer who builds websites gave Claude Code a baseline site, access to Google, X, LinkedIn and Reddit ad accounts with a budget, plus Apify and OpenRouter. The site personalizes content per visitor using device, location and behavior signals rendered via DeepSeek. Claude Code reviews and acts every four hours.
how_it_went: The author says it is mostly doing tomfoolery so far: generating lots of SEO pages and adding share buttons, which he compares to what interns suggest. He still finds watching its decisions fun.
worth_knowing: The site reads around fifty device signals and can search public profiles from autofilled names, so it gates everything behind a consent page with an erase option. Giving an agent live ad spend means real money is on the line.
prompt: Every 4 hours, review [your website repo] and its analytics, then propose up to three changes to the site or to my ad campaigns on [ad platforms] within a total budget of [budget]. Explain the reasoning for each change. Show me the plan and any ad spend changes and wait for my approval before deploying site changes or changing campaigns.

curation.rationale: A real autonomous experiment where Claude Code runs a website and ad accounts on a 4-hour loop, but results are thin and anecdotal. The heavy visitor-profiling design adds privacy concerns, though the site discloses it and asks consent.
